title: Merlinhawk Aerospace and Boeing Sign Deal to Service Indian Navy's P-8I Fleet From Bengaluru
excerpt: The partnership will provide in-country maintenance for advanced electro-optical systems, reducing downtime and supporting India's Atmanirbhar Bharat defence manufacturing push.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Merlinhawk Aerospace partners with Boeing to service Indian Navy's P-8I fleet in Bengaluru.
  • The deal enhances in-country maintenance for advanced electro-optical systems, reducing overseas dependency.
  • The P-8I fleet has surpassed 40,000 flight hours, crucial for Indo-Pacific maritime security.
  • This partnership supports India's Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative for self-reliant defence manufacturing.

Merlinhawk Aerospace, a Bengaluru-based aerospace and defence technology company, has signed an agreement with Boeing India Defence to provide in-country sustainment support for advanced electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) systems deployed on defence platforms in India.

The Deal

Under the agreement, Merlinhawk will leverage its L3Harris WESCAM Authorized Service Centre (WASC) in Bengaluru to deliver maintenance, repair, technical support, and lifecycle sustainment for the advanced sensor systems. The arrangement is designed to reduce turnaround times and keep critical defence assets mission-ready without shipping components overseas for servicing.

"The Indian Navy's P-8I fleet is a cornerstone of maritime security in the Indo-Pacific," said Nikhil Joshi, Managing Director of Boeing Defence India. "Collaborations such as these enable faster turnaround, higher fleet availability, and greater mission readiness for the Indian Navy."

India's Maritime Backbone

The Indian Navy operates 12 P-8I aircraft — the Indian variant of Boeing's P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft — which have collectively surpassed 40,000 flight hours. The fleet provides long-range maritime reconnaissance and anti-submarine warfare capabilities across the Indian Ocean Region and broader Indo-Pacific.

Keeping these aircraft at peak operational readiness requires sophisticated sensor maintenance that was previously dependent on overseas service facilities. The Merlinhawk partnership brings that capability in-house.

"As defence platforms become increasingly technology-intensive, the ability to provide responsive, in-country lifecycle support becomes mission critical."

— Karthik Ramineni, CEO, Merlinhawk Aerospace

Atmanirbhar Defence

The partnership fits squarely within the Modi government's Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) initiative for defence manufacturing. India has been steadily building indigenous MRO capabilities to reduce dependence on foreign service providers and position itself as a regional aerospace maintenance hub.

Boeing's broader India strategy, centered on its BIRDS (Boeing India Repair Development and Sustainment) hub launched in 2021, includes multiple Indian companies supporting engineering, maintenance, and sustainment services for both defence and commercial aircraft. The Merlinhawk deal extends that network into the specialized domain of electro-optical systems.

For India's growing defence export ambitions and the thousands of Indian-origin professionals working in the global aerospace sector, the deal represents another step toward India being taken seriously as a player in defence technology servicing — not just as a buyer of foreign platforms, but as a capable partner in maintaining them.

›Aims to reduce reliance on foreign service providers.
›Positions India as a regional aerospace MRO hub.
›Enhances local capabilities for maintenance and repair.
